stories.title: I-043 -- shutdown-splash terminal reason not observable
acceptance: [I-043] the shutdown splash cannot observe/render the terminal reason (clean shutdown vs cutoff). Wire the ShutdownSequencer terminal reason to the shutdown splash so it renders honestly; never a fabricated reason. ruff clean
stories.completionNotes:
SHIPPED. All four terminal exits of shutdown-state-poll.js now report WHY, on two sinks: a console line (-> chromium stderr -> `journalctl -u splash-grace.service`, grep `[shutdown-splash] terminal`) and a zero-paint `data-terminal-*` attribute pair on <body>. The report carries the SEQUENCER's own phase+reason (lifted off the last shutdown-state actually read) alongside the splash's local cause -- two different facts, both named, neither substituted for the other. Causes: cancelled | state-missing | black-tail-cap | unrecognized-phase.

READ THIS BEFORE REVIEWING THE AC WORDING. The AC says 'renders honestly'; I did NOT add a visible render, and that is deliberate, not a narrowed scope. I-043's own text forbids it: 'US-525 deliberately did not patch the render side... forcing a paint when the state says the shutdown is over would be a dishonest instrument -- the opposite of the rule the splash exists to serve', and its stated requirement is '`journalctl -u splash-grace.service` ALONE should say which of the four terminal cases fired', with 'prefer the console route'. Spec 6 also requires cancelled/unrecognized to abort with NO fadeout, so painting a reason would contradict the phase contract. The DOM attribute is the 'renders' half done at zero paint cost. If PM/Atlas wants a VISIBLE reason, that is a separate call and reverses an explicit Atlas/US-525 decision.

MECHANISM, NOT JUST DECLARATION -- the part most likely to be reverted by someone who does not know why it is there: chromium DISCARDS web-content console output unless the unit passes `--enable-logging=stderr`, so the JS half ALONE would have been an elaborate no-op on the Pi. Both grace units (x11 + wayland) now carry that flag with the reasoning in their headers. NO `--log-level` is pinned on purpose: chromium logs web-content console messages at INFO regardless of which console method is used, so raising the threshold would filter out the very line the flag exists to surface. `--remote-debugging-port` explicitly NOT adopted alongside it (US-522 -- unauthenticated DevTools on a car-mounted kiosk) and is fenced by a test.

NEW TEST INFRASTRUCTURE: tests/ui/shutdown_probe.js -- the closeout splash had no node probe (the boot splash had splash_probe.js since US-499), which is not a coincidence: its only observable WAS window.close(), identical on all four paths. The probe captures console output byte-for-byte, so the tests assert the string the operator actually greps. runShutdownSplash() added to render_harness.py.

4 MUTATIONS, all reverted BY HAND and confirmed byte-exact via `git diff --numstat` (wayland +14/-0, x11 +15/-1, i.e. pure additions, no mutation residue): (A) bare abort() -> 3 RED incl. the static no-silent-exit fence. (B) drop --enable-logging=stderr from the wayland unit -> 1 RED, and the x11 variant stayed GREEN, which also proves the header COMMENT mentioning the flag does not satisfy the guard (the US-501/US-513 prose trap -- the parser has its own self-test with a positive control). (C) fabricate phase='cancelled' when no state was ever read -> 1 RED on the honest-instrument test. (D) collapse state-missing into cancelled -> 2 RED, headed by test_theFourTerminalCauses_areDistinguishableFromEachOther. (D) is the one that matters: the defect was never 'nothing is logged', it was 'a correct abort and a race are indistinguishable', so a single generic reason string would pass a naive did-it-log test and leave I-043 fully open. Distinctness is the property, so distinctness is what is asserted.

GATE: targeted = tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_terminal_reason.py (15) + the 4 neighbouring suites that share these artifacts (test_shutdown_splash_render, test_splash_min_visible_floor, pi/splash/test_shutdown_splash_wiring, deploy/test_splash_kit) -- 53 passed, EXIT 0. ruff clean on both touched .py files (`make` is not on PATH on this box, exit 127 reads like a pass -- use `python -m ruff check <file>`). FOR PM: full suite is yours at integration; my diff touches no src/, only the shipped kit + tests.

STILL OWED (Pi-side, not closable on the dev box): the validationCriteria drill. The console->journal leg is the ONE link no headless test can prove -- the probe proves the line is emitted, the unit test proves the flag is set, but only `journalctl -u splash-grace.service` on the Pi proves chromium actually forwards it. Do that on the next clean shutdown BEFORE spending a real AC-loss event on it.

stories.title: I-044 -- kiosk XDG_RUNTIME_DIR %U expands to 0 (root) in the splash/dashboard units
acceptance: [I-044] the kiosk systemd units' XDG_RUNTIME_DIR uses %U which expands to 0 (root) -> /run/user/0 permission errors (dconf/dbus). Set it to the real autologin user's runtime dir (/run/user/<uid>). ruff clean; no /run/user/0 permission errors in the journal
stories.completionNotes:
SHIPPED. `%U` -> `__PI_UID__` on all 5 kiosk units that declare XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, substituted at install time by a new V-4 probe (`id -u $PI_USER`) in both kit installers, alongside the existing __PI_USER__ (V-1) and __CHROMIUM_BIN__ (V-3) seams. Dry-run now renders the resolved runtime dir: `/run/user/1000` for mcornelison, which is exactly what `ls -d /run/user/*` reports on the box.

THE SET IS 5, NOT THE 6 I-044 LISTED -- dashboard.service.x11 never declared XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (X11 needs only DISPLAY). The issue's own 'confirm the set, do not assume this list is complete' caveat was right. So the guard DISCOVERS units by globbing both kit dirs rather than reading a list, and pins the discovered count -- a unit added later is covered the day it lands, and a glob that silently stops matching fails loudly instead of passing an absence check over an empty list.

*** TOOL BLINDSPOT WORTH MORE THAN THIS STORY: the Grep tool found ZERO of the five defect sites. *** specs/UI/dist/ is gitignored-but-tracked, and ripgrep honours .gitignore, so a completeness sweep for `%U` via Grep returns clean over a repo where every single instance is present. I would have concluded 'already fixed' on the strength of an empty result. `git grep` searches tracked files and found all five instantly. Any audit of specs/UI/dist/ (the entire shipped UI kit) MUST use git grep. This generalises: an empty search result is only evidence if you know the tool can see the files.

FAIL-LOUD, NEVER 0: an unresolvable uid ABORTS the install. A fallback would re-create I-044 silently -- the unit installs, chromium starts, and only the journal knows. V-4 deliberately runs LAST of the four probes so V-1/V-2/V-3's aborts keep their precedence (they answer 'can we install at all'; V-4 answers 'can we render it correctly'), which also left the sibling kits' unknown-session tests asserting the message they were written for.

4 MUTATIONS, all reverted BY HAND, byte-exact per `git diff --numstat` (every unit file reads +N/-1 = the one Environment line plus header, no residue). (A) one unit back to %U -> 2 RED naming the file. (B) drop the __PI_UID__ sed from render_unit -> 1 RED, and it is the instructive one: the installer still PRINTED 'Resolved user UID: 4242' while shipping a literal `/run/user/__PI_UID__`, and my static test (placeholder + `id -u` + FORCE_UID all appear in the file) stayed GREEN, because those strings survive in comments. Declaration vs mechanism again -- the end-to-end dry-run render is the only assertion that means anything. (D) parser returns {} -> 3 RED headed by the positive control.

*** (C) IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: IT PASSED, AND THAT WAS A REAL GAP IN MY OWN TEST. *** I mutated the probe to `id -u ... || echo 0` -- the exact silent-fallback the story exists to forbid -- and the suite stayed GREEN. Cause: my fail-loud test forced FORCE_UID empty, which short-circuits at the override branch and never runs `id -u` at all. It tested the mock, not the mechanism. Added test_installer_failsLoudWhenIdUItselfFails, which unsets FORCE_UID and names a user that cannot exist, so the REAL probe runs and really fails -- the actual production mode. Under mutation C it goes RED and prints `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/0`, i.e. reproduces I-044. A forced-override test proves the override works; it says nothing about the path that runs on the Pi.

TOKENIZED, NOT SUBSTRING (US-522 lesson, false-POSITIVE direction this time): the fixed units now explain %U in their headers on purpose, so `'%U' not in text` would FAIL on a correct file. The guard parses Environment= assignments (comments stripped first, continuations joined) and asserts on the VALUE. Since the headline assertion is an ABSENCE, the parser carries a positive control (must still FIND /run/user/%U when planted) plus a negative one (a commented-out directive must NOT parse as live) -- mutation D proves both earn their keep.

COLLATERAL, FLAGGED NOT HIDDEN: 3 existing test files needed the same one-line treatment V-3 got when it landed -- V-4 is a new mandatory install-time probe and the forced users in those suites ('pi', 'tunerbox') do not exist on a dev box, so `id -u` fails and the installer aborts before reaching what they assert. test_splash_kit/test_dashboard_kit got `env.setdefault(*_FORCE_UID, '1000')` next to the existing FORCE_CHROMIUM setdefault; test_kiosk_install's _runInstaller sets it explicitly. No assertion was weakened. Also de-duplicated the substitution set into one `render_unit()` per installer -- it was about to become a third copy of the same sed, which is how a placeholder gets added to the install path and not the dry-run path.

GATE: targeted = tests/deploy/test_kiosk_runtime_dir.py (16) + the 4 suites that share these artifacts (test_kiosk_install, test_splash_kit, test_dashboard_kit, test_deploy_pi) -- 140 passed, EXIT 0, re-run green after all reverts. ruff clean on all 4 touched .py files (`make` is not on PATH -- exit 127 READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check <file>`). FOR PM: full suite is yours at integration; my diff touches no src/, only the shipped UI kit + tests.

STILL OWED (Pi-side, uncloseable here, and it is the whole point of I-044): this repo can prove the installer RENDERS /run/user/1000; only the box can prove systemd RESOLVES it. After deploy+boot: `systemctl show splash-boot.service -p Environment -p User` (expect /run/user/1000, not /run/user/0) and `journalctl -u splash-boot.service` clean of dconf/'Could not parse server address'. Assert against `systemctl show`, NOT the unit text -- trusting the unit text is why this issue existed.

stories.title: Pi<->server schema/contract PARITY GUARD (A-4) -- standing CI test
stories.completionNotes:
SHIPPED. scripts/audit_sync_contract_parity.py (pure check functions + CLI, pattern of audit_address_mirrors.py) driven by tests/lint/test_pi_server_contract_parity.py (71 tests). All 6 assertions land as A1-A6. Table set is sync_log.PK_COLUMN UNION snapshot_registry.SNAPSHOT_SYNC, computed per call -- complete-by-construction, pinned by a test that registers a new table via monkeypatch and asserts it appears with no edit to the guard. I unioned SNAPSHOT_SYNC in beyond the DoD's named PK_COLUMN because US-416 added a SECOND wire path (startup_log); a guard watching one path would report parity over a table set that is not the synced set.

*** THE GUARD FOUND 3 REAL DIVERGENCES ON ITS FIRST RUN -- read this before assuming it was written to fit a green repo. *** (1) A4: drive_summary's PK is drive_id and the client HAS been renaming it since US-206, but schema_diff.PI_PK_RENAMED_TO_ID never declared it -- exactly the 'new synced table added without its mapping' case the AC names. Fixed (the declaration, not the behaviour; the client derives the rename from PK_COLUMN and was always correct). (2+3) A3 flagged dtc_freeze_frame's data_source + vehicle_info_vin as unmapped. Those are TRUE facts but my stated CONSEQUENCE was wrong: that table does not use the generic bind path, it has a bespoke cross-tier resolver (US-369 api/sync._syncDtcFreezeFrameRows) that renames vehicle_info_vin -> vehicle_info_id and intentionally drops data_source. So the wire model was incomplete, not the code. Fixed by declaring the THIRD transform (CROSS_TIER_RESOLVED_COLUMNS) rather than widening an exemption until the noise stopped.

*** THE ONE DELIBERATE AC DEVIATION -- FLAGGED, NOT SILENTLY NARROWED; PM/ATLAS OWN THE CALL: offices/pm/inbox/2026-08-10-from-ralph-us543-data-quality-parity-needs-atlas-ruling.md. *** AC #1 says data_source AND data_quality set-equality both ways. data_source is implemented exactly so. data_quality is NOT a shared contract today: Pi={full,clock_unsynced} (US-419 clock-drift flag, WIRE-STRIPPED by sync_log._WIRE_STRIPPED_COLUMNS), server={full,attribution_anomaly,foreign_vehicle,sparse,below_threshold,unmappable_legacy} (drive-level analytics), and server power_log/startup_log have NO data_quality column at all -- B-104's 'Pi = emitter, server = authority'. Flat set-equality would assert a falsehood and force one tier to adopt the other's vocabulary. So the check is CONDITIONAL: while the column is wire-stripped, parity is not required and the STRIP is asserted; the day it is un-stripped the check flips to full set-equality both ways. That is the same failure mode (a Pi-only value reaching a server that does not know it), asserted where it can actually occur.

5 MUTATIONS, all reverted BY HAND, byte-exact per git diff --numstat (sync_log.py shows NO diff; schema_diff.py reads +14/-0, pure addition). (A) drop the drive_summary rename declaration -> 3 RED. (B) THE ONE THAT PROVES THE CONDITIONAL HAS TEETH: remove data_quality from _WIRE_STRIPPED_COLUMNS -> 5 RED, headed by A1 naming the full vocabulary divergence in both directions PLUS A3 on power_log and startup_log (the two tables whose pushes would start being rejected). A conditional check nobody has watched fire is just a disabled check. (C) skip ObdDatabase.initialize() in the Pi loader -> 8 RED, incl. the populated-ColumnSpec positive control, so an empty/degenerate load cannot pass vacuously. (D) widen CROSS_TIER_RESOLVED_COLUMNS with a bogus realtime_data.value exemption -> 4 RED via the self-policing 'declared dropped but the server HAS that column' check: the one hand-written exemption cannot be quietly widened into a hole.

AC #2 (applied, NOT Python constants) is the load-bearing one and is honest about its two halves. Pi: fully applied, always-on -- loadPiAppliedSchema() runs the REAL ObdDatabase.initialize() (every ensureX helper) against a throwaway SQLite file and reads PRAGMA table_info. That is not a stylistic choice: schema_diff's DDL-constant loader cannot see dtc_freeze_frame AT ALL (it is a hand-listed registry and that table arrives via ensureDtcFreezeFrameTable), so a constants-based guard would have reported clean over a synced table it never loaded. Asserted, not assumed, by test_appliedLoader_seesASyncedTableTheDdlLoaderCannot -- if the two loaders ever agree, that test fails and tells you to re-justify the expensive path. Server: applied via the US-464/470 real-MariaDB harness (information_schema), which SKIPS honestly on the bench (no Docker/testcontainers). Its verdict logic is proven hermetically (missing table / missing column / EMPTY column dict all RED), and checkContractParity provably does NOT substitute the models for the applied schema when the DB is absent -- A2 simply does not run, pinned by a test.

AC #6 is a ROUND TRIP, not a declaration: the exact string utcIsoNow() emits is pushed through the server's own api/sync._parseDateTime, which must return a datetime. If it ever passes the string through (what a trailing-'Z' or fromisoformat regression looks like) the raw text lands in a DateTime column with NO error raised. Alarm proven by monkeypatching _parseDateTime to a passthrough.

TOKENIZED, NOT SUBSTRING -- I walked straight into the trap my own last two stories warned about, and it cost a red test: my design guard asserted `'create_all' not in source`, which FAILED because the audit module DOCUMENTS the create_all trap in its header. Same US-522 lesson, false-positive direction again. Fixed with an ast walk over Name/Attribute/alias nodes (comments + docstrings are not code), carrying a positive control (a planted Base.metadata.create_all IS detected) and a negative one (the same text in a comment is NOT).

FILED, NOT ABSORBED: TD-079 -- schema_diff.loadPiSchema's hand-listed DDL registry is blind to dtc_freeze_frame and to every future ensureX-only table, so the TD-039 drift gate has been reporting 'shared tables clean' over a synced table it cannot see. Out of this story's scope (Rule 3); the fix is an adapter job because the two loaders return different shapes.

GATE: targeted = tests/lint/ (71 new + the A-15 mirror suite) + the 5 suites sharing these artifacts (test_schema_diff, test_sync_log_pk_variants, test_data_source_foreign_marker, test_data_source_applied_schema_accepts_foreign, test_sync_client) -- ALL PASSED across 3 synchronous runs, EXIT 0, green again after every revert. ruff clean on all 3 touched .py files (`make` is not on PATH -- exit 127 READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check <file>`). FOR PM: full suite is yours at integration -- my diff touches src/ NOT AT ALL (the only non-test production edit is +14/-0 of declaration/comment in scripts/schema_diff.py), so regression risk is low, but tests/scripts/test_schema_diff.py is the one suite worth a second look since I changed a constant it reads.

CI WIRING IS THE OPEN QUESTION FOR PM: this is a 'standing CI test' and it currently stands only as a pytest file. It runs in the normal suite (tests/lint/), which is the same footing as the A-15 mirror gate it copies. If 'standing CI' means something stronger here (pre-commit hook, deploy-gate invocation of `python scripts/audit_sync_contract_parity.py`), that wiring is a PM/deploy call I did not make unilaterally. The A2 applied-server layer additionally needs testcontainers+Docker (or $OBD2_MARIADB_TEST_DSN) to stop skipping -- the same CI-enablement follow-up US-464 already owes.
acceptance: [Atlas A-4 contract list 2026-08-10] a standing CI test (pattern of scripts/audit_address_mirrors.py) asserting Pi<->server agree on the shared contract -- 6 assertions:
1. ENUM PARITY: data_source AND data_quality value-sets IDENTICAL Pi<->server (set-equality both ways). Source of the A-10 saga (Pi got 'foreign', server didn't)

2. APPLIED-SCHEMA NOT PYTHON-TUPLE (US-459 lesson, LOAD-BEARING): assert the APPLIED schema -- server via the real-MariaDB testcontainer (US-464/470), Pi via the SQLite DDL after ensure-schema runs -- NOT the Python constants. A tuple-only test ships green over a broken DB (the drift this guards)

3. SYNCED-TABLE SHARED-COLUMN PARITY: for every table in sync_log.PK_COLUMN, the sync-payload columns exist on BOTH tiers with compatible types. Tier-LOCAL columns (server source_device/source_id, Pi bookkeeping) exempt -- assert the SYNCED surface only

4. PK-RENAME MAPPING PARITY: every synced table's Pi-PK -> server-id rename (sync client map; e.g. battery_health_log drain_event_id->id) is DECLARED + consistent -- catches a new synced table added without its mapping

5. Pi ENSURE-SCHEMA COVERAGE (not a schema_migrations table): every shared/synced column the server declares has a corresponding Pi ensureXSchema helper/DDL column. Pi's ensureXSchema IS its migration equivalent; guard it stays in sync with the server's shared surface
6. TIMESTAMP/FORMAT PARITY: synced timestamp columns use canonical ISO-8601 UTC on both tiers (TD-027/US-202); the sync does no coercion beyond the PK rename, so a format divergence corrupts silently

DoD: name sync_log.PK_COLUMN as the table set (complete-by-construction -- a future synced table auto-covered); run assertion #2 against the US-470 testcontainer + the Pi SQLite DDL. This GUARDS (F-076 normalizes; this keeps it normalized). ruff clean

stories.title: OBD BT bond self-heal + boot verify (A-18 follow-on)
acceptance: [Atlas addition A-18] on boot / on repeated connect-fail, detect a lost-or-de-bonded state (bonded=no) and auto-run the re-pair path (or loudly surface it) -- never silent capture-death. Include the BT-stack-wedge reset (power off/on + longer scan) that was needed 2026-08-07. verify_bt_pair.sh exists -- wire it into the reconnect path.

[Atlas refinement -- serialize re-pair vs the port] auto-re-pair MUST stop/hold eclipse-obd's connection first (systemctl stop eclipse-obd before pairing) -- never pair while the logger contends on the port ('multiple access' hazard from 2026-08-07)
[Atlas refinement -- bounded, not a loop] cap auto-re-pair (once per boot / backoff) -- never re-pair on EVERY connect-fail (hammers the radio)

[Atlas refinement -- loud-surface when not discoverable] unattended auto-re-pair only works if the dongle is discoverable+unbonded; if discovery does not find it, do NOT silently retry -- surface it (state/log) so the operator power-cycles the dongle (honest-instrument)

validationCriteria.action: clear the bond on the Pi, then boot / attempt capture
validationCriteria.outcome: the Pi detects bonded=no and auto-re-pairs (or loudly surfaces it); capture recovers rather than silently dying

stories.goal: As the operator, I want the Pi to detect + auto-recover a lost BT bond instead of silently dying on capture, so the month-long bond outage cannot recur unnoticed.
